integration.instructions: Place official NASA files in resources/incoming/, add them to this manifest, then follow docs/RESOURCE-INTEGRATION.md.

sources.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 official challenge resource pack
sources.notes: The official pack has not been supplied in this workspace. Current values are gameplay-balanced provisional estimates. Drop official files into resources/incoming/ and map their fields before claiming official data status.

sources.name: Space Mission Concept Development Using Concept Maturity Levels
sources.citation: Wessen, R. R., Borden, C., Ziemer, J., & Kwok, J. (2013). Space Mission Concept Development Using Concept Maturity Levels. IEEE Aerospace Conference.
sources.notes: CML 1-4 definitions were adapted into a game badge. The app labels this as a game adaptation, not an official NASA assessment.

sources.name: Design and Develop Science Missions
sources.notes: Used for the mission-segment discipline spine (science, spacecraft, launch, ground, operations) and review/closure framing. It is not a source of numerical component data.

sources.name: CubeSat 101: Basic Concepts and Processes for First-Time CubeSat Developers
sources.notes: Used as supporting guidance for small-spacecraft process, reviews, integration and test, and risk language. Numerical values are not taken directly from this guide.

sources.name: NASA Goddard Mission Design Lab discipline set
sources.notes: Inspired the mass equipment list, power/data budgets, orbit analysis, launch accommodations, risk and cost review structure. The game is an independent prototype, not an official MDL product.

sources.name: NASA mission-viz
sources.notes: Evaluated for a Three.js mission visualization. The current single-player build uses a dependency-light SVG orrery and flight track; a mission-viz adapter would be a post-v1 enhancement and must preserve the zero-backend constraint or run as a static asset.

sources.name: James Webb Space Telescope: Build It Yourself
sources.notes: Used for architecture trade-off framing and real-mission analogue references. No assets, code, or text were copied from the Webb game.

sources.name: General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT)
sources.notes: GMAT is not embedded. The app downloads a starting .script for Earth, Moon, Mars and Venus, or a JSON orbit-element set where GMAT lacks a stock central body. Force model and frame must be re-validated in GMAT.

fieldMappings.fallback: Provisional gameplay-balanced values; see dataset status in the app.

releaseChecklist: Official NASA Space Apps resource pack supplied with usage terms recorded.
Every official file listed in sources[].files and copied into resources/incoming/.
Field mappings reviewed; sourceIds point at recorded sources.
Provisional values replaced or explicitly marked mixed/official in src/data/dataset.ts.
DataStatusModal and README updated to match the new status.
npm test and npm run build pass.
